transcript:
[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda: cost econ review, results from last week's profiling, and next steps.
[00:08] Maya Lopez: thanks Alex, yeah we want to focus on how this maps to our finance targets \u0014 Leila's on the call.
[00:14] Leila Haddad: hi all, thanks \u0014 we got the spreadsheet but need better numbers for $/1k tokens and realistic tail latencies.
[00:20] Priya Singh: cool, Priya here \u0014 i ran the baseline today again with the sample workload you sent, ran hosted r/w variant and recorded tokens per second per dollar and tail stats.
[00:28] Daniel Park: quick note \u0014 our peak QPS comes between 1pm-3pm PT, roughly 1200 requests/minute, average prompt length ~110 tokens, response ~320 tokens.
[00:37] Alex Morgan: perfect, that helps. priya, can you just summarize the headline numbers?
[00:41] Priya Singh: yup. baselined on the r/w-13b-quant model \u0014 hosted pricing assumptions we used: $X per 1k tokens (redacted in notes), but normalized metric we shared was tokens/sec per dollar. for the baseline (no caching, batch=1) we saw ~4.6k tokens per $ and p95 latency ~420ms for a single stream.
[01:02] Maya Lopez: 4.6k tokens per dollar, ok \u0014 how does that compare with the cached runs?
[01:06] Priya Singh: with prefix/KV cache enabled and our workload's 42% repeated prefixes we saw effective savings of ~30% token cost \u0014 so tokens/sec/$ bumped to ~6.5k effective tokens per $ when accounting for cache hits. note the cache hit rate is workload dependent, we used the sample set you provided.
[01:25] Leila Haddad: 30% is big. is that consistent across longer sessions?
[01:29] Priya Singh: it's variable \u0014 for sessions with high prompt reuse you can go up to 40-45%, but in cold-start conversations it's closer to baseline. average for your data looked like that ~30.
[01:39] Alex Morgan: another axis is batching \u0014 we did batch profiling. priya?
[01:43] Priya Singh: yeah. batching increases throughput, so tokens/sec/$ goes up, but you pay a latency tax. sample numbers: batch=4 gave ~2.1x throughput improvement (so tokens/sec/$ ~9.7k) with p95 increasing to ~560ms; batch=8 gave ~3.6x throughput (~16.6k tokens/$) with p95 ~780ms. those p95 are for the end-to-end path we measured (including network).
[02:10] Daniel Park: so at batch=8 we get great cost efficiency but p95 is almost double \u0014 that could violate our SLOs. our product needs p95 <600ms for search/autocomplete flows.
[02:22] Priya Singh: exactly \u0014 recommendation is mixed strategy: keep batch=1 for latency-sensitive endpoints (search/autocomplete) and enable batching for background generation (emails, summaries). Redwood's routing can split by route.
[02:36] Maya Lopez: what about model variants / quantization? we looked at some 8-bit quantized variants last week.
[02:42] Priya Singh: good question. quantized 8-bit reduces cost per token by ~25% in our perf runs but sometimes costs a small quality delta \u0014 in your eval set we saw negligible drop on intent classification but slight regression on long-form summarization for outlier docs. also quantized models tend to have slightly different latency profiles, sometimes faster per-token but less predictable for very long sequences.
[03:05] Leila Haddad: so stacking caching + batching + quantization \u0014 what is the combined $/1k tokens ballpark?
[03:11] Priya Singh: with caching (30% effective skip), batching for background (avg across mixed traffic), and 8-bit quantization for non-critical flows, your blended outcome was ~20-35k tokens per $ effective, which translates to roughly 30-50% lower unit cost vs baseline hosted. i'll caveat: exact $/1k depends on your share of latency-sensitive traffic.
[03:35] Alex Morgan: that's helpful. Leila, does that fit the finance target range?
[03:39] Leila Haddad: our target is to get below current vendor spend \u0014 we're targeting $/1k tokens that's 40% less than our incumbent. these numbers could work but need line-item transparency for procurement.
[03:50] Daniel Park: technical question \u0014 how warm does the KV cache need to be? we have lots of ephemeral sessions.
[03:56] Priya Singh: kv cache warmup depends on user stickiness. we measured hit-rate ramp after ~15-30 requests per conversation in your sample, which is typical for our shopping-assistant flows. for ephemeral sessions, caching still saves prefixes from product/sku prompts that repeat across users (e.g., promo descriptions).
[04:16] Maya Lopez: any downside to aggressive caching? memory footprint?
[04:19] Priya Singh: yes memory and eviction policies matter. on dedicated you can provision larger cache with more predictable eviction; on hosted we maintain reasonable TTLs. also some customers have data residency concerns if cache stores user content \u0014 we offer encryption and TTL controls and you can opt out for PII flows.
[04:38] Alex Morgan: procurement/security came up \u0014 i know you had a security review with infra last week?
[04:42] Daniel Park: yes, we still want SOC2 docs and SSO integration details.
[04:45] Alex Morgan: noted \u0014 i'll share our security pack after this call. see action items.
[04:50] Maya Lopez: two more items: 1) routing policies \u0014 how do we do canary/fallback? 2) Fall back model cost if dedicated capacity is exhausted?
[04:59] Priya Singh: for routing we support policy-based routing: latency-priority routes use lower-batch, reserved pathways. fallback can go to cheaper quantized models or to a hosted burst pool. for cost calc we included a sample fallback scenario in the spreadsheet where fallback to quantized reduces cost but increases error-rate slightly.
[05:18] Leila Haddad: can you show the spreadsheet numbers live?
[05:21] Alex Morgan: i put a link in the chat \u0014 open the cost_econ_v3 sheet.
[05:24] [05:24] Screen-share/brief silence while doc opened
[05:35] Priya Singh: pointing at sheet: Row 12 is baseline tokens/$, row 18 is cached scenario, row 24 is batching blended. see column F for blended per-route split. the assumptions tab shows prompt/response distributions used \u0014 these came from Daniel's export.
[05:49] Daniel Park: those distributions look right. can we add a peak-hour multiplier to show worst-case spend?
[05:53] Priya Singh: yes we can, will add peak multiplier to the sheet and re-run the blended calc.
[05:58] Maya Lopez: another ask \u0014 can you run a p99 analysis? procurement cares about tail risk.
[06:02] Priya Singh: i can run p99 but need longer traces; i'll pull 48 hours of logs and run the p99 profiles and include in next update.
[06:12] Alex Morgan: timeline check: procurement timeline and dedicated capacity commit?
[06:15] Leila Haddad: we'd like to finalize vendor by end of month, and nailing down cost numbers this week is important for the finance review.
[06:23] Alex Morgan: ok we'll prioritize the spreadsheet update and the profiling runs.
[06:26] Daniel Park: curious \u0014 any note on tokens/sec/$ vs competitor? you mentioned Anthropic in earlier thread.
[06:31] Priya Singh: vendor-to-vendor comparisons are noisy; for similar model sizes we saw our serving perf similar to public bench, but caching + dedicated allocation tends to widen the economic advantage because other vendors don't expose the same caching controls. we'll add a short comparison note.
[06:48] Maya Lopez: Anything about autoscaling and burst pricing? we've seen big cost spikes.
[06:52] Alex Morgan: Redwood Dedicated has reserved pools + burst with predictable pricing \u0014 we included a burst cost column in the sheet. if you want tight cost control you can set burst caps and auto-fallback.
[07:04] Leila Haddad: need to see a sample SLA and can we get a commitment around latency percentiles?
[07:09] Alex Morgan: standard Dedicated SLA includes p95 latency targets for reserved capacity, we'll share the SLA doc. p99 commitments are higher tier \u0014 we'll include options.
[07:17] Daniel Park: minor transcription note \u0014 in the previous run some names in logs were mangled, hope that won't affect profiling.
[07:23] Priya Singh: no, logs map back to request IDs.
[07:26] Maya Lopez: ok let's recap next steps.
[07:29] Alex Morgan: recap: Alex will share updated security pack + pricing by Friday (2025-11-07). Priya will run batch=8 and batch=16 profiles and p99 runs, update the spreadsheet (due 2025-11-07). Daniel will share exact token distribution and peak windows (due 2025-11-08). Maya/Leila will confirm finance targets and procurement timeline (due 2025-11-10).
[07:51] Leila Haddad: sounds good \u0014 thanks team.
[07:54] Alex Morgan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in slack with the sheet link. bye.
[07:58] [End of recording]
